source: An adaptation is a body part or behavior that helps a living thing survive where it lives: a camel's hump of fat, a duck's webbed feet, a cactus's spines and waxy skin, birds flying south.
Thinking an animal grows an adaptation because it needs it. Adaptations are passed down from parents over many generations.
A polar bear has thick fur and a layer of fat. A camel can go days without drinking. Each is built for the place it lives.
An adaptation is a body part or a behavior that helps a living thing survive and have young where it lives.
Adaptations help each living thing fit its home.
Some adaptations are behaviors: bears hibernate, birds migrate, possums play dead. Camouflage (colors that hide) and mimicry (looking like something dangerous) are adaptations too.
An animal has a long sticky tongue and strong claws for digging. What might it eat?
Ants or termites (it is an anteater).
Claws dig into nests; a sticky tongue picks up tiny things.

Thinking an animal grows an adaptation because it wants or needs it. A giraffe does not stretch its neck longer by trying. Adaptations are passed down from parents to young over many, many generations.
